title: H1 Retest Before Bearish Continuation
description: Gold is trading around 3,949, extending its recovery from the recent 3,87x low after a sharp liquidation phase. The rebound has been supported by softer oil prices and a slightly weaker dollar, but the broader macro environment remains restrictive. The Fed held rates at 3.75%–4.00% last week, while inflation remains elevated and December tightening expectations are still significant. Technical View The H1 structure remains bearish despite the current rebound. Gold previously shifted from the upper channel through a clear CHoCH, followed by strong bearish displacement through the Fibonacci retracement structure and into the 3,87x area. Price has since produced a short-term bullish reaction and is now holding inside the 3,938–3,956 Current Demand Zone. This recovery can extend further, but the key technical test sits higher at 3,984–4,003 Retest / Reaction Zone. That area overlaps with the previous breakdown structure and represents the strongest nearby location to evaluate whether sellers are ready to regain control. Key Zones 4,068–4,084 — Major Supply Zone 3,984–4,003 — Retest / Reaction Zone 3,938–3,956 — Current Demand Zone 3,868–3,883 — Major Downside Target Trading Plan Sell Priority The main scenario is to allow Gold to extend its corrective recovery from the 3,938–3,956 Current Demand Zone toward 3,984–4,003 Retest / Reaction Zone. Condition: price reaches the retest zone but fails to establish sustained H1 acceptance above 4,003, followed by renewed bearish confirmation. If sellers regain control from this area, I will favor a rotation back through 3,938–3,956. A decisive breakdown below current demand would then reopen the path toward the 3,868–3,883 Major Downside Target. The projected sequence is: 3,938–3,956 hold → corrective rally into 3,984–4,003 → bearish rejection → continuation toward 3,868–3,883. Important Note Gold has already rebounded sharply from deeply oversold conditions, so the current recovery should not automatically be interpreted as a structural bullish reversal. Today’s U.S. JOLTS release and Friday’s October employment report are the next important labor-market catalysts and could create sharp volatility around the marked zones. A sustained H1 reclaim above 4,003 would weaken the immediate bearish continuation thesis and increase the probability of a deeper recovery. Sell View The sell-side view remains preferred, but location matters. Selling directly around 3,949 offers less structural advantage while price is still recovering from demand. The cleaner bearish POI is 3,984–4,003, where the rebound meets previous breakdown structure. Final View Gold is recovering, but the broader H1 structure has not yet turned bullish. The immediate 3,938–3,956 demand zone is supporting the current bounce, while 3,984–4,003 remains the real directional test. If sellers defend that retest zone, the chart continues to favor renewed downside pressure toward 3,868–3,883. For now, the approach remains simple: let price complete the retracement first, then judge whether sellers are ready to resume control.

title: Checking the Possibility of Support and Pullback Formation
description: Hello, traders! It's great to see you all. Make sure to "Follow" to stay updated with the latest information. Have a great day! ------------------------------------- https://www.tradingview.com/x/F7BCOkw8/ To continue the upward wave, we need to see whether the price can find support near the M-Signal indicator on the 1M chart and move higher. We also need to observe whether the price can remain within the current brick while buying pressure strengthens. https://www.tradingview.com/x/fZTEj01K/ After falling below the M-Signal indicator on the 1M chart, the price attempted to recover above it but failed. Subsequently, the price found support near the 59981.47 ~ 66323.12 range and moved higher, eventually breaking above the M-Signal indicator on the 1M chart. Now that the price has returned to the vicinity of the M-Signal indicator on the 1M chart, the key question is whether it can establish support and form a pullback pattern. It would be ideal if the price continued rising immediately after breaking above an important level or range, but such cases are relatively rare. In most cases, the price tends to retest the breakout level as support before continuing its upward movement. This type of pattern is commonly referred to as a Cup and Handle pattern because the price movement resembles a cup with a handle. At this point, I believe the most ideal bottom for the pullback would be near 69978.65. The reason is that this level is close to where the HA-Low indicator first appeared on the 1W chart. If the price declines too much, selling pressure could increase and potentially trigger a sharp drop. Therefore, the formation of this pattern may take some time. One concern, however, is that capital flows remain unfavorable. https://www.tradingview.com/x/RO6jNp9V/ https://www.tradingview.com/x/LujgjkA7/ I believe the downward gaps in USDT and USDC indicate that capital is flowing out of the cryptocurrency market. Therefore, while the Cup and Handle pattern is forming, we need to watch whether capital begins flowing back into the market. If the outflows do not develop into a chain reaction, I expect the market may be able to defend key price levels even when strong selling pressure emerges. Looking at historical price movements, the current market behavior can be interpreted as the early stage of an upward trend. Therefore, I believe this may be a time to gradually accumulate positions from a medium- to long-term investment perspective. However, buying does not simply mean continuously adding to positions. It is essential to make purchases strategically to lower the average entry price. If you do not have enough time to monitor the market closely, gradually buying small amounts before a bearish candle closes may also be a useful approach. --- Thank you for reading until the end. I wish you successful trading. --------------------------------------------------

title: ETHUSDT 1H: if/then plan for a pullback into the OTE zone
description: ETH has made a break of structure off the 30 Oct low. I'm not chasing it. Here is exactly what I need to see on the pullback before I look for a long. The bigger picture The sell-off on 30 Oct took price through monthly support at 2,257.79 and wicked far below it. Price has since climbed back and is testing that line from below. What just happened From the 30 Oct low, ETH rallied to a high on 2 Nov and broke above the earlier swing highs. That is a break of structure. I draw my Fibonacci backwards: the 0 sits at the low where the move began, and the 1 at the high where it ended. My pullback zone runs from the 0.382 line down to the 0.236 line, with the sweet spot at 0.295. This is the optimal trade entry zone, the area where I'm willing to look for a long. Price is still above it. The white line shows the path I'm watching: a small bounce, a pullback into the zone, then a push above the high of the move. The plan: IF THIS, THEN THAT IF price pulls back into the 0.382 to 0.236 zone in a corrective way: small, choppy, overlapping candles, not a sharp drop AND the confluence stacks up inside the zone: it sweeps the earlier lows, it sits on a 4H or daily level, and the zone is tight THEN I'll look for a leveraged long on the first close back above the sweep candle's high, on the 15 minute or 1 hour chart. A sweep is when price briefly takes out an earlier low to trigger stop orders, then turns back. Confluence means several reasons lining up in one place. The close back above the sweep candle is called a CHoCH, a change of character. IF price drops in a sharp, one-way move through the zone, THEN there is no trade. IF price rallies to the 1 without pulling back, THEN there is no trade. I do not chase. IF price breaks below the 0, the 30 Oct low, THEN the setup is void. Where it could go I'm looking for the end of the bigger move, not a quick bounce. I expect the pullback within a day or two and the push that follows to take a few days. This is my analysis of the chart, not financial advice. Leverage multiplies losses as well as gains. Size your risk so being wrong is small.
